To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
infusional chemotherapy costs more than bolus chemotherapy in all cases.

infusional administration is more expensive for 4/5 regimens (cisplatin, 5‐fluorouracil, doxorubicin, and cyclophosphamide), and that bolus administration is more expensive than infusional administration for methotrexate in the treatment of breast cancer.
the cost of infusinal chemotherapy is not significantly more expensive than bolus chemotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a model of projected costs for the administration of chemotherapy regimens in the treatment of three of the most common cancers, colorectal, breast, and non-small cell lung cancer, using both bolus and continuous infusion schedules.

the development of a model of the projected charges as a base for the cost estimate of selected common chemotherapy regiments for comparison of the cost based on the charges for bolus vs. infusion chemotherapy schedules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the projected charges for the infusional chemotherapy regimens are not significantly different from those for the bolus regimens.
there is no evidence to support the contention that infusional chemotherapy is more expensive than the bolus schedule.
the cost of infusion therapy is more expensive than bolus therapy based on the analysis of charges.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
infusional administration is not necessarily more expensive than the bolus schedule.
infusional delivery of chemotherapy for the regimens studied is not more costly than the bolus schedule.
the cost of infusinal administration of selected chemotherapy regimens is comparable or even less expensive than the cost of bolus administration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cost of infusively administered chemotherapy is less than that of bolus chemotherapy.
the cost difference is not as large as many people believe.
there is a cost advantage for infusional chemotherapy in the majority of the chemotherapy regimens studied.
